name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Friday 1 April 1977

clue.text: Burke's accomplice imprisoned of course

blocks.note: to jug someone is slang for putting them in jail
William Hare was the partner of William Burke in the Edinburgh body-snatching murders of 1828

explanation.surface: A history note: the partner of the murderer Burke was, naturally, locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like a filler meaning 'naturally'; it is the definition, read as 'served as a course of a meal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jugged hare is a traditional British dish of hare stewed in a pot, so it is something eaten as one course of dinner.

clue.text: Vehicle for the magistrate about mid-week

indicators.note: mid- points to the centre of the word it is attached to, keeping only the middle letters
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: JP stands for Justice of the Peace, a lay magistrate
the two central letters of week

explanation.surface: Someone asks which car the local magistrate will need around Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeep is a small rugged motor vehicle, first built for the US Army.

clue.text: Degree held in French was hands for Tommys

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece is gripped within the other

blocks.note: a grade is a degree or level
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A garbled remark about a degree, the French language and British soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed definition looks garbled, probably 'was handy for Tommies'. Tommies are British soldiers, from Tommy Atkins, and the hand grenade was a staple of their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, a standard weapon of the British infantryman.

clue.text: No shoe-siring production this fantastic show

definitions.text: No shoe-siring production this fantastic show

blocks.note: surface reading: a show that was not put on cheaply
setter's reading: a lavish spectacular, the opposite of a shoestring budget production

explanation.walkthrough: 'shoe-siring' is a misprint for 'shoe-string': a shoestring production is one made on a tiny budget, so this is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravaganza is an elaborate, costly theatrical entertainment, exactly what a no-expense-spared fantastic show is.

clue.text: Car seat fitting could be earthed, inserting point

indicators.note: could be suggests the word may be rearranged into something it is not yet
inserting means pushing one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An electrician wonders whether a fitting in the car seat could be earthed by adding a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-rest is the padded support attached to the top of a car seat behind the occupant's head.

clue.text: What remains on the head of the widow

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a relic is something surviving from the past
first letter of the

explanation.surface: Something left behind sits on a widow's head, like a mourning cap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second. Note the answer itself can also mean 'what remains'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an old legal and literary word for a woman whose husband has died, the one left behind.

clue.text: Point to Marlowe's burlesque

blocks.note: S, south, is a compass point
the Elizabethan playwright Christopher Marlowe was known as Kit

explanation.surface: A literary note pointing to a comic piece by Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that parodies something, which is what a burlesque does.

clue.text: Look for rising, including record one for water-spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up
including means taking something inside

blocks.note: to look for something is to seek it
LP, long-player, is a vinyl record
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone searches the hills, with a record in hand, for water-spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The record and the one sit together between the two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelpies are shape-shifting water-spirits of Scottish folklore, often appearing as horses near lochs and rivers.

clue.text: Twisted necklace upset first male inquisitor

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word is flipped bottom to top

blocks.note: a torque, or torc, is a neck ring of twisted metal worn by ancient Celts
in Genesis Adam is the first man

explanation.surface: A tangled necklace annoys the first man to wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomás de Torquemada was the first Grand Inquisitor of the Spanish Inquisition, notorious for its cruelty.

clue.text: Even Cicero comprehends article at last

indicators.note: to comprehend can mean to include or take in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written
Marcus Tullius Cicero was traditionally called Tully in English
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Even the great Roman orator finally understands a piece of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means in the end, after a delay, which is what 'at last' expresses.

clue.text: Fuzzy effect of most of a book's publicity'.'

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a blurb is the promotional text on a book's cover

explanation.surface: A complaint that a book's advertising leaves only a vague impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen indistinctly, without sharp outlines, which is a fuzzy effect.

clue.text: What's left to a fellow he should receive 9

blocks.note: the remainder is what is left over
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A will leaves the leftovers to some fellow, who will get them in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9-across, EVENTUALLY, so the definition reads 'he should receive eventually'.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a remainderman is the person who inherits an estate only after an earlier interest, such as a life tenancy, ends.

clue.text: Party returns to a lake in Wales

indicators.note: returns means goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of holidaymakers goes back to a Welsh lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bala Lake, Llyn Tegid, in Gwynedd is the largest natural lake in Wales.

clue.text: No poor locality for this cardinal

blocks.note: riche is French for rich, the opposite of poor
lieu is French for place, as in the English phrase 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: A wealthy district is fitting for a churchman of high rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French words, fitting for a French cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Richelieu was Louis XIII's chief minister, the most famous cardinal in French history.

clue.text: Cards falsified by 300 entries

indicators.note: falsified means doctored or tampered with, so the letters are changed around

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so three of them make 300
taken as written

explanation.surface: Playing cards or record cards have been faked by three hundred false entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cards' looks like playing cards or index cards; it is the old slang for odd characters.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is informal for an amusing or odd person, so cards are eccentrics.

clue.text: Split caused by clergyman taking donkey into church

indicators.note: into means put inside, so the first pieces go within the last

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title
an ass is a donkey
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar leads a donkey into church, perhaps on Palm Sunday, and causes a rift.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack or fissure in a glacier, a split in the ice.

clue.text: Healer cures a lamb's indisposition

indicators.note: indisposition is illness, a state of being out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written with the s

explanation.surface: A vet or healer treats a lamb that is feeling poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a soothing aromatic resin or ointment used to heal wounds, so it is a healer.

clue.text: Comforted when put on ice round the poles

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: putting something on ice cools it
N and S are the North and South poles

explanation.surface: Someone was soothed when ice was applied, or when sent to the polar ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on ice' suggests postponed, but here it is literal chilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To console is to comfort someone in grief or disappointment.

clue.text: Observation begins with unusual perception

blocks.note: the definition: the act of spotting or watching
setter's reading: the word starts with ESP, extrasensory perception, an unusual way of perceiving

explanation.surface: Good observation starts from an unusually sharp eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Not full wordplay: the clue simply notes that the answer opens with the abbreviation for extrasensory perception.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for the act of catching sight of something, or of spying, so it is observation.

clue.text: Interrogate relatives of fairy coach-maker

blocks.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently for information
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Police question the family of a fairy-tale coach-builder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cinderella the fairy godmother turns a pumpkin into a coach, so it is what the coach was made from.

clue.text: Like Dobson's road-crossing Rose

blocks.note: surface reading: a flower, perhaps a rose variety, spreading across a road
setter's reading: in Austin Dobson's triolet 'Urceus Exit', Rose crosses the road in her latest new hat

explanation.walkthrough: Austin Dobson was a Victorian writer of light verse; in his triolet the poet's ode becomes a sonnet because 'Rose cross'd the road / In her latest new bonnet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose was wearing a bonnet, so she was a lady with a bonnet on her head.

clue.text: Live first in the air with Roman officer

indicators.note: first in means placed inside near the front, so one piece is set within the other

blocks.note: an air is a tune or melody
the printed word looks like a misprint, probably for 'Rib', which is taken as written

explanation.surface: A garbled line about living in the open air alongside a Roman officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue seems corrupt: 'Live' cannot supply the needed letters, so the original word was most likely 'Rib'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribune was an official of ancient Rome, either a military officer of a legion or a magistrate protecting the plebs.

clue.text: Blue as an archaeologist with a nil result

blocks.note: an archaeologist at work is in a dig, an excavation
a score of nil is written O

explanation.surface: A disappointed archaeologist feels blue after finding nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a mood, sad after a fruitless dig; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep violet-blue colour, named after the dye from the indigo plant.

clue.text: Different longitudes reduce men to sue

indicators.note: to reduce something is to break it down and convert it into another form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the printed word appears to be a misprint for 'size', as in the phrase cut down to size

explanation.surface: Probably 'reduce men to size': putting arrogant people in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'sue' must be 'size' to supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Time zones are bands of the globe between lines of longitude, each keeping its own clock time.

clue.text: Heroic tale depicted herein

indicators.note: herein means inside this, telling you the letters are found within the word beside it

blocks.note: letters two to five of depicted

explanation.surface: A heroic story is portrayed in this very piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem about the deeds of heroes, such as the Iliad.

clue.text: What a cat docs in a stable yard

blocks.note: first meaning: makes a cat's cry (docs is a misprint for does)
second meaning: a row of stables round a yard, now often homes

explanation.surface: A cat is miaowing in the stable yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat makes a high plaintive cry, and a set of stables arranged around a yard or lane is also called by this name.

clue.text: What's black in Kentucky'.'

blocks.note: taken as written
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is dark in the state of Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means black as ink, stained or coloured dark like ink.

clue.text: Small creature filmed maybe by a river

indicators.note: maybe hints the word is only one possible version, so its letters can take another arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
the Ouse is the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: A wildlife cameraman films a small animal on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A field mouse is a small wild rodent of fields and woodland, a classic small creature.

clue.text: Seaside George

blocks.note: first meaning: what a beach is made of
second meaning: the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Seaside George' sounds like a holidaymaker's nickname; the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaches are covered in fine grains of rock, and the nineteenth-century French novelist wrote as George Sand.

clue.text: Those making smaller wireless parts'

blocks.note: first meaning: things or people that compress or shorten
second meaning: capacitors, components found in a radio set

explanation.walkthrough: A wireless is the old British word for a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to make shorter or denser, and capacitors were long called by this name in radio engineering.
